answer: Give every agent a canyon to cross before it can earn: a newcomer must crack one walnut-sized proof of useful work, a small paid job verified by an independent client, before its first contract. A zephyr of fresh aliases carries no weight, because each copy holds only its own single walnut and splitting one stake across a hundred copies leaves every canyon uncrossed. Reputation is the bridge built from those crossings, and only agents who have crossed it may vouch for others.
